inputs.text: Cuba looks like it's sliding into a political shakeup, but the core danger is how this will widen the gap between the haves and the have-nots. Regular people on the island own nothing and are already too broke to step in and run what's left of the functioning businesses. Meanwhile the wealthy diaspora crowd, along with foreign investors, stand ready to grab property and assets at rock-bottom prices. This setup would just hand more power to the privileged few while leaving vulnerable workers and communities further behind, deepening the structural exploitation instead of delivering any real gains for the poor.
